items.stem:
The exchange rate between euros and dollars is
1 euro = 1.15 dollars.

parts.t: Change 250 euros into dollars.
Change 92 dollars into euros.

sols: one euro is worth more than one dollar, so the number of dollars must be larger
this is the reverse of part (a)

items.stem:
The exchange rate between euros and rupees is
1 euro = 82.4 rupees.

parts.t: Change 350 euros into rupees.

Change 5000 rupees into euros.
Give your answer correct to 2 decimal places.

sols: the third decimal place is 9, so round up
Check: 60.68 × 82.4 = 5000.03, which is 5000 to the nearest rupee ✓

items.stem:
Nadia travels from the United States to Mexico.
She changes 500 dollars into pesos when the exchange rate is 1 dollar = 17.6 pesos.

parts.t: Work out the number of pesos she receives.

Nadia spends 6200 pesos. At the end of her holiday she changes all the pesos she has left back into dollars, when the exchange rate is 1 dollar = 17.9 pesos.
Calculate the number of dollars she receives.
Give your answer correct to 2 decimal places.

sols: Pesos → dollars, so divide by the new rate 17.9.
she is changing money the other way, and the rate has changed

items.stem:
The same model of camera is on sale in two countries.
In the United States it costs 410 dollars.
In France it costs 372 euros.
The exchange rate is 1 euro = 1.08 dollars.

parts.t: Change 372 euros into dollars.
Work out the difference between the two prices, in dollars.
Write down the country in which the camera is cheaper.

ms:
B1
FT, must be consistent with their (a)
sols: both prices are now in the same currency
The French price is $401.76 and the American price is $410.00.

items.stem:
Thabo changes 3000 rand into dollars.
The bank first takes a commission of 2% of the 3000 rand, and then changes the rand that are left at the rate 1 dollar = 18.25 rand.

parts.t: Calculate the commission, in rand.

Calculate the number of dollars Thabo receives.
Give your answer correct to 2 decimal places.

ms:
M1 for 3000 − their 60 (= 2940) oe, or 0.98 × 3000
M1 for their 2940 ÷ 18.25
A1
accept 161.0958… seen, FT their (a)

items.stem:
On Monday the exchange rate was 1 pound = 1.32 dollars.
On Friday the exchange rate was 1 pound = 1.29 dollars.

parts.t:
Calculate the percentage decrease in the value of the pound against the dollar from Monday to Friday.
Give your answer correct to 3 significant figures.

Sam changes 600 dollars into pounds on Friday instead of on Monday.
Calculate how many more pounds he receives.
Give your answer correct to 2 decimal places.

sols: Decrease in value = 1.32 − 1.29 = 0.03 dollars per pound.
percentage change is always measured against the original value
dollars → pounds, so divide by the rate
the pound is weaker on Friday, so each dollar buys more pounds

items.stem:
The exchange rates for the dollar are
1 dollar = 0.92 euros  and  1 dollar = 7.80 yuan.

parts.t:
Find the exchange rate 1 euro = k yuan.
Give the value of k correct to 2 decimal places.

Change 2500 yuan into euros.
Give your answer correct to 2 decimal places.

ms:
M1 for 2500 × 0.92 ÷ 7.80 oe, or 2500 ÷ 8.4782…
A1
accept 294.871… seen; 294.81 from using 8.48 scores M1 only
sols: Take 1 dollar as the link between the two currencies.
1 dollar = 0.92 euros and 1 dollar = 7.80 yuan, so 0.92 euros = 7.80 yuan.
both are worth exactly one dollar
use the unrounded rate throughout, then round only at the end

items.stem:
A bank in Cairo displays two rates for the dollar.
When the bank sells dollars: 1 dollar = 31.2 Egyptian pounds.
When the bank buys dollars: 1 dollar = 30.6 Egyptian pounds.
Yara takes 9360 Egyptian pounds to the bank and buys dollars.

parts.t: Calculate the number of dollars Yara receives.

Her trip is cancelled, so she immediately sells all of these dollars back to the same bank.
Calculate how many Egyptian pounds she has lost.

sols: Yara is buying dollars, so the bank is selling them: use 1 dollar = 31.2.
always use the rate for the direction the bank is trading
Selling the dollars back, the bank buys them at 1 dollar = 30.6.
the gap between the buying and selling rates is how the bank makes its money

items.stem:
Layla flies from Japan to Kenya, changing planes in Germany.
The exchange rates are
1 euro = 160 yen  and  1 euro = 142.5 shillings.
In Japan she changes 96 000 yen into euros.

parts.t: Work out the number of euros she receives.

In Germany she spends 215 euros. She changes all the euros she has left into shillings.
Calculate the number of shillings she receives.

In Kenya she buys a wooden carving costing 18 000 shillings.
Calculate the cost of the carving in yen.
Give your answer correct to 3 significant figures.

ms:
M1 for 18 000 ÷ 142.5 × 160 oe
A1
accept 20 210.5… seen, cao for the 3 s.f. value
sols: the euro is the link currency between shillings and yen
20 210.5… rounds to 20 200 because the third significant figure is 2 and the next digit is 1

items.stem:
A jacket costs 63 pounds in London and 79 dollars in New York.
The exchange rate is 1 dollar = 0.84 pounds.

parts.t:
Work out the difference between the two prices.
Give your answer in pounds.
Write down the city in which the jacket is cheaper.

Later the New York price increases by 8% and the exchange rate changes to 1 dollar = 0.81 pounds.
Calculate the new New York price in pounds.
Give your answer correct to 2 decimal places.

ms:
M1 for 79 × 0.84
A1 for 66.36
A1 for 3.36
alternative: M1 for 63 ÷ 0.84 (= 75), A1, A1 for 4 dollars → 3.36 pounds

B1
FT, must be consistent with their (a)
sols: Change the New York price into pounds: dollars → pounds, so multiply by 0.84.
both prices are now in pounds
London costs £63 and New York costs £66.36.
an 8% increase is a multiplier of 1.08
Dollars → pounds at the new rate: 85.32 × 0.81 = 69.1092

items.stem:
A bank in Tokyo displays the exchange rate
100 yen = 0.61 euros.

parts.t: Change 25 000 yen into euros.

Change 200 euros into yen.
Give your answer correct to the nearest yen.

ms:
M1 for 200 ÷ 0.61 × 100 oe or 200 ÷ 0.0061
A1
accept 32 786.88… seen; 32 786 or 32 790 scores M1 only
sols: 100 yen = 0.61 euros, so 25 000 yen is 250 lots of 100 yen.
0.61 euros = 100 yen, so 1 euro = 100 ÷ 0.61 yen = 163.93… yen
divide both sides by 0.61 to find the value of one euro

items.stem: Priya changes 240 euros into dollars and receives 312 dollars.

parts.t:
Find the exchange rate.
Give your answer in the form 1 euro = … dollars.

Leo changes 550 euros into dollars at the same rate.
Work out how many dollars Leo receives.

sols: divide both sides by 240 to find the value of one euro

items.stem: The exchange rate is 1 dirham = 0.27 dollars.

parts.t:
Find the exchange rate in the form 1 dollar = … dirhams.
Give your answer correct to 3 significant figures.

Change 150 dollars into dirhams.
Give your answer correct to the nearest dirham.

ms:
M1 for 150 ÷ 0.27 oe
A1
accept 555.5… seen; 555 from 150 × 3.70 scores M1 only
sols: use the exact rate, not the rounded 3.70, to avoid a rounding error

items.stem:
A bureau de change charges a fixed fee of 5 dollars for every transaction.
It then changes the remaining money at the rate 1 dollar = 0.92 euros.
Rashid takes 240 dollars to the bureau to change into euros.

parts.t: Calculate the number of euros Rashid receives.
Work out how many euros the fixed fee cost him.

sols: the fee is taken off before the exchange
The fee of 5 dollars is worth 5 × 0.92 euros.

items.stem:
Chen changes 375 dollars into euros at the rate 1 dollar = 0.88 euros.
The bank only has 20-euro notes, so it gives Chen as many 20-euro notes as it can and gives him the rest of the money in coins.

parts.t: Work out the value, in euros, of the 375 dollars.
Work out the number of 20-euro notes Chen receives.
Work out how much money Chen receives in coins.

sols: The bank cannot give half a note, so Chen gets 16 notes.
round down: 16 notes are worth 320 euros, 17 would be 340 euros which is too much

items.stem:
In Spain petrol costs 1.65 euros per litre.
In Canada petrol costs 1.72 Canadian dollars per litre.
The exchange rate is 1 euro = 1.48 Canadian dollars.

parts.t: Show that petrol is cheaper in Canada than in Spain.

Amina buys 45 litres of petrol in Canada.
Calculate the cost in euros.
Give your answer correct to 2 decimal places.

ms:
M1 for 1.65 × 1.48 (= 2.442) or 1.72 ÷ 1.48 (= 1.162…)
A1 for correct comparison and conclusion

M1 for 45 × 1.72 ÷ 1.48 oe or 77.4 seen
A1
accept 52.297… seen
sols: Change the Spanish price into Canadian dollars so the two prices are in the same currency.
2.442 > 1.72, so a litre costs less in Canada. Cheaper in Canada.
alternatively 1.72 ÷ 1.48 = 1.16 euros per litre, which is less than 1.65

items.stem:
Marta works in Lisbon. She is paid 14.50 euros per hour and works 35 hours each week.
The exchange rate is 1 euro = 1.12 dollars.

parts.t: Calculate Marta's weekly pay in dollars.

Marta saves one quarter of her weekly pay every week.
She wants to save enough to buy a laptop costing 2000 dollars.
Work out the smallest number of weeks she must save for.

ms:
M1 for their 568.40 ÷ 4 (= 142.10) or 2000 ÷ their 568.40 × 4
M1 for 2000 ÷ their 142.10 (= 14.07…)
A1 cao
14 or 14.1 scores M2 only
sols: one quarter of the weekly pay
After 14 weeks she has 14 × 142.10 = 1989.40 dollars, which is not enough.
round up: a whole number of weeks is needed and 14 is too few

items.stem:
In January the exchange rate was 1 pound = 1.25 dollars.
By June the value of the pound against the dollar had increased by 4%.

parts.t:
Find the exchange rate in June.
Give your answer in the form 1 pound = … dollars.

Ben changes 250 pounds into dollars in June.
Calculate how many more dollars he receives than if he had changed the 250 pounds in January.

ms:
M1 for 250 × their 1.30 − 250 × 1.25 oe, or 250 × 0.05
A1
FT their (a), accept 12.5
sols: A 4% increase is a multiplier of 1.04.
each pound now buys 5 cents more

items.stem:
Ahmed takes some dollars to a bank to change into euros.
The bank keeps 4% of the dollars as commission and changes the rest at the rate 1 dollar = 0.92 euros.
Ahmed receives 828 euros.

parts.t: Work out the number of dollars the bank changed into euros.
Work out the number of dollars Ahmed gave to the bank.
Work out the commission, in dollars.

ms:
M1 for their 900 ÷ 0.96 oe
A1
FT their (a); 936 from 900 × 1.04 scores M0

B1
FT their (b) − their (a), or 4% of their (b)
sols: The 900 dollars is what is left after 4% is taken, so it is 96% of the original amount.
reverse percentage: divide by the multiplier
not 900 × 1.04 = 936, because 4% of the original is more than 4% of 900

items.stem:
Two bureaux de change offer to change pounds into dollars.
Bureau A: 1 pound = 1.28 dollars, no fee.
Bureau B: 1 pound = 1.31 dollars, then a fee of 6 dollars is deducted.

parts.t: Kofi changes 150 pounds. Show that he receives more dollars from Bureau A and work out how many more.
Find the number of pounds that would give the same number of dollars from both bureaux.

ms:
M1 for 150 × 1.28 (= 192)
M1 for 150 × 1.31 − 6 (= 190.5)
A1 for 1.50 with A stated as better
sols: the fee comes off after the exchange
192.00 > 190.50 so Bureau A gives more, by 192.00 − 190.50 = $1.50
Let x pounds be changed. Bureau A gives 1.28x and Bureau B gives 1.31x − 6.

items.stem: The graph can be used to convert between pounds (£) and dollars ($).

parts.t: Use the graph to change 24 pounds into dollars.
Use the graph to change 45 dollars into pounds.
Use the graph to find the exchange rate, and hence change 640 pounds into dollars.

ms:
M1 for a rate of 1.25 (oe, e.g. 40 → 50 or 8 → 10 read from the graph) or 640 × their rate
A1
accept 790 to 810 from a consistent graph reading
sols: Find 24 on the pounds axis, go up to the line, then across to the dollars axis.
Find 45 on the dollars axis, go across to the line, then down to the pounds axis.
Read a convenient point: 40 pounds = 50 dollars.
use a point far from the origin so the reading is accurate
640 is off the graph, so use the rate rather than reading directly

items.stem:
Sofia hires a car in Italy. The cost is 45 euros per day plus 0.12 euros for each kilometre driven.
She hires the car for 6 days and drives 350 km.
The exchange rate is 1 euro = 1.09 dollars.

parts.t: Calculate the total cost of the hire, in euros.
Calculate the total cost in dollars.

Sofia had budgeted 350 dollars for the car hire.
Work out the greatest number of extra whole kilometres she could have driven without going over her budget.

ms:
M1 for 350 ÷ 1.09 (= 321.10…) − their 312, or (350 − their 340.08) ÷ 1.09 ÷ 0.12
A1 cao
76 or 75.8 scores M1 only
sols: Money left for extra kilometres = 321.10… − 312 = 9.10… euros
round down: 76 km would cost 9.12 euros, more than the 9.10 euros available

items.stem:
A bank displays these rates for changing between dollars and euros.
When the bank sells euros: 1 dollar = 0.90 euros, and a fixed fee of 4 euros is deducted.
When the bank buys euros: 1 dollar = 0.93 euros, with no fee.
Diego changes 500 dollars into euros.

parts.t: Calculate the number of euros Diego receives.

Diego's trip is cancelled and he immediately sells all his euros back to the bank.
Calculate the number of dollars he receives.
Give your answer correct to 2 decimal places.

Calculate his overall percentage loss on the 500 dollars.
Give your answer correct to 3 significant figures.

ms:
M1 for their 446 ÷ 0.93
A1
FT their (a); accept 479.569… seen

M1 for (500 − their 479.57) ÷ 500 × 100 oe
A1
FT their (b); accept 4.086… seen
sols: Diego is buying euros, so the bank is selling euros: use 1 dollar = 0.90 euros.
Now the bank is buying euros back at 1 dollar = 0.93 euros.
always use the rate for the direction the bank is trading
percentage change is measured against the original 500 dollars

items.stem:
Kwame lives in South Africa. In March he changes 29 600 rand into dollars when the exchange rate is 1 dollar = 14.8 rand.
In September he changes all of these dollars back into rand when the exchange rate is 1 dollar = 16.1 rand.

parts.t: Work out the number of dollars Kwame buys in March.

Calculate his percentage profit.
Give your answer correct to 3 significant figures.

Kwame's friend Lindiwe does the same, using the same two exchange rates, and makes a profit of exactly 1000 rand.
Calculate the number of dollars Lindiwe bought in March.
Give your answer correct to 2 decimal places.

ms:
M1 for their 2000 × 16.1 (= 32 200)
M1 for (their 32 200 − 29 600) ÷ 29 600 × 100 oe
A1
alternative: M2 for (16.1 − 14.8) ÷ 14.8 × 100; accept 8.783… seen
sols: dollars → rand, multiply by the new rate
measured against the 29 600 rand he started with
check: each dollar gained 1.3 rand, and 1.3 ÷ 14.8 × 100 = 8.78% ✓
Each dollar is bought for 14.8 rand and sold for 16.1 rand, a profit of 1.3 rand per dollar.
Let d be the number of dollars: 1.3d = 1000

items.stem:
A video game is sold in the United States. Its price is quoted in dollars.
In March the exchange rate is 1 dollar = 0.79 pounds.
Between March and October the price of the game in dollars increases by 5%, and the exchange rate changes so that each dollar is worth 3% more pounds.

parts.t: Calculate the percentage increase, from March to October, in the price of the game in pounds.

In March the price of the game in pounds was £53.72.
Work out its price in dollars in March.

ms:
M1 for 1.05 and 1.03 seen as multipliers
M1 for 1.05 × 1.03 (= 1.0815) oe
A1
8 (adding the percentages) scores 0
sols: Price in pounds = (price in dollars) × (pounds per dollar).
The dollar price is multiplied by 1.05 and the pounds-per-dollar rate is multiplied by 1.03.
multipliers combine by multiplying, not adding
